tiktok_title: Newborn bisa ngantuk lagi sejam setelah bangun. Contekan wake window 0-18 bulan
caption:
Newborn bisa udah ngantuk lagi 1-1,5 jam setelah bangun, dan waktu nyusu ikut dihitung. Makin besar, makin lama kuat melek: 6-12 bulan sekitar 2-3 jam, mendekati 1 tahun 3-4 jam.

Angka wake window ini kisaran kasar, bukan pedoman resmi dokter anak. Yang nomor satu tetap tanda ngantuknya: menguap, tatapan kosong, tarik telinga, rewel. Tidurkan selalu telentang, di kasur datar tanpa bantal dan selimut.

Total tidur sehari semalam: 0-3 bulan 14-17 jam (WHO), 4-12 bulan 12-16 jam, 1-2 tahun 11-14 jam (AASM, didukung AAP).

Bayimu sekarang kuat melek berapa lama?

Sumber: WHO 2019, AASM 2016, Raising Children Network, Tresillian

sources: Raising Children Network (Australian Government funded), Tired signs in babies: newborns may get tired as soon as 1-1.5 hours after waking, some stay happy 2 hours or more. 3-6 months tired after 1.5-3 hours awake. 6-12 months after 2-3 hours. Newborn tired signs: pulling at ears, closing fists, yawning, staring into space, jerky arm and leg movements or arching backwards, frowning. Baby signs: clinginess, grizzling or crying, boredom with toys. https://raisingchildren.net.au/babies/sleep/understanding-sleep/tired-signs and https://raisingchildren.net.au/newborns/sleep/understanding-sleep/tired-signs

Tresillian (NSW child and family health), daily routines: 4-6 weeks average awake time 1-2 hours, 7-12 weeks 1-2.5 hours, including feed and play. 6-8 months 2-3 hours. 9-10 months 2.5-3.5 hours. 11-12 months 3-4 hours. around 14 months many move to one nap. https://www.tresillian.org.au/newborn/routines/ , https://www.tresillian.org.au/baby/sleep/7-to-12-months/ , https://www.tresillian.org.au/baby/routines/9-to-12-months/

Plunket (NZ), Sleep 1-2 years: most toddlers go from two naps to one between 12 and 18 months. example day implies longer awake stretches with one nap. https://www.plunket.org.nz/child-development/sleep/sleep-1-2-years/sleep-1-2-years/

WHO 2019, Guidelines on physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep for children under 5: 0-3 months 14-17 h, 4-11 months 12-16 h, 1-2 years 11-14 h, including naps. https://www.who.int/news/item/24-04-2019-to-grow-up-healthy-children-need-to-sit-less-and-play-more

AASM pediatric consensus 2016 (Paruthi et al., J Clin Sleep Med), endorsed by AAP: 4-12 months 12-16 h, 1-2 years 11-14 h per 24 h including naps. no recommendation under 4 months. https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/685231
Wake windows are not part of AAP or AASM guidance. pediatric sleep physician Craig Canapari notes little evidence behind them. https://drcraigcanapari.com/wake-windows
notes: SHORT format (4 slides). Wake-window numbers are rough ranges from Raising Children Network and Tresillian, labelled 'kisaran kasar' on the slide and 'bukan pedoman resmi dokter anak' in the caption. 12-18 months has no published range in our sources: '3 jam lebih' is the 11-12 month floor (Tresillian 3-4 h) and grows with the switch to one nap (Plunket). Totals: WHO for 0-3 months (AASM has none under 4 months), AASM/WHO after. Crib art: telentang, flat empty mattress.
